title: Cocktail 2 Pours This Friday. It's Shahid, Kriti, Rashmika — and the First 'A'-Rated Film of Kriti Sanon's Career.
excerpt: Fourteen years after Saif and Deepika set the template for the urban Bollywood rom-com, Homi Adajania remixes it with three of the biggest names in the business — a chartbuster Pritam soundtrack, an adults-only certificate, and 11,000 tickets sold before the bar even opened.
body:
The original Cocktail dropped in 2012 and quietly rewrote what a Hindi rom-com could look like: Ibiza beaches, a Saif Ali Khan caught between two women, and a debutante named Diana Penty holding her own against the full force of peak Deepika Padukone. It was glossy, it was grown-up, it was the kind of film NRIs put on at house parties for the next decade. Fourteen years later, the bar reopens — and the new round is stronger.

Cocktail 2 hits cinemas worldwide this Friday, June 19, and director Homi Adajania — back behind the camera, with Dinesh Vijan's Maddock Films producing again — has loaded it with the kind of casting that makes a trailer launch feel like an event. Shahid Kapoor as Kunal. Kriti Sanon as Ally. Rashmika Mandanna as Diya. Three relationships, one tangle of friendship and romance, and a love triangle that the censors clearly decided wasn't for the kids.

Because here's the headline that's lighting up timelines: the Central Board of Film Certification has stamped Cocktail 2 with an 'A' certificate. Adults only. And for Kriti Sanon — twelve years into a career built on glossy, mainstream charm — this is, remarkably, her first adult-rated film. For Rashmika, it's her second after the blistering Animal (2023). For Shahid, who has practically built a parallel filmography out of edgier fare, it's his fifth, after Kaminey, Udta Punjab, Kabir Singh, and his last release O'Romeo. That makes Cocktail 2 the first time in his career he's strung two adults-only films back to back.

What does an 'A'-rated rom-com even look like in 2026? The studio's keeping the censor notes under wraps, but the runtime tells its own story — at 150 minutes, Cocktail 2 runs four minutes longer than the original, and the buzz around the soundtrack suggests this is a film that wants to seduce before it scandalizes.

Ah, the soundtrack. Pritam is on music, and at a pre-release event in Mumbai back in May, the team teased two tracks that have already become the film's calling card. 'Mashooka' — picture Shahid romancing Kriti across Sicily, all playful, goofy energy building to a frankly seductive dance break. And 'Tujhko' — an Arijit Singh ballad for Shahid and Rashmika, the slow-burn number that hints their characters were college sweethearts pulled apart by circumstance. When the team asked the assembled press which song should drop first, the room voted Mashooka. Pritam, ever the romantic, insisted they honor the verdict.

The early numbers suggest the audience is just as eager. Advance booking opened at the stroke of midnight on June 14, and within the first 24 hours Cocktail 2 had moved roughly 11,000 tickets for opening day — strong, especially in the urban multiplex circuits where romantic entertainers traditionally thrive. Trade analysts are projecting a ₹12–15 crore opening in India, which would comfortably outpace the first film's ₹10.95 crore debut and crown Cocktail 2 among the better Bollywood openers of the year. There's even chatter it could top Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar's ₹15.73 crore as the biggest post-pandemic rom-com opening. Fittingly, that record also belongs to a Maddock-adjacent glossy romance — the genre clearly knows its own.

Shahid, for his part, sounds like a man enjoying himself. "After very long I'm playing an extremely likeable, warm and endearing character," he said of Kunal — a pointed pivot after the brooding intensity of his recent roles. After Kabir Singh's rage and O'Romeo's edge, watching Shahid Kapoor simply be charming again might be the film's quietest pleasure.

The glamour wattage peaks Thursday, when the cast — Shahid, Kriti, Rashmika, Adajania, and Vijan — descend on Delhi for what's being billed as one of the capital's starriest premieres in recent memory, with the film's singers and composers expected to turn up too. Given how much the music carries this story, that's less a red carpet than a concert.

For the diaspora, the where-to-watch is the easy part: Maddock's romances open day-and-date across the US, UK, Canada, and Australia, so Cocktail 2 lands in theatres near you the same Friday it opens in Mumbai. The 'A' certificate applies in India; international ratings will vary by territory, but expect it pitched firmly at grown-ups who remember the first film fondly and have been waiting fourteen years for the next round.

The urban rom-com has spent the post-pandemic years being declared dead more times than anyone can count. Cocktail 2 is betting that three magnetic leads, a Pritam album, and a little adult-rated mischief are exactly the cure. Pour it Friday and find out.
